[Bug][A3] DeepSeek-V4.1: missing causal_conv1d_update_npu -> CausalConv1dBwd ACL-graph crash kills decode EngineCores · Issue #18304 · vllm-project/vllm-ascend · GitHub (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/18304)
citeturn57search2 [wordlim: 200] Published: last month; Crawled: last month; `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_triton.py` still tries to bind `causal_conv1d_update_npu` for the KDA layers (its comment notes the PyTorch fallback "calls .item() per request, which aborts ACL graph capture"), but that kernel was deleted from `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/causal_conv1d.py` by PR #14620 ("[Refactor][Ops] Remove causal_conv1d_update_npu", merged 2026-08-25). ...      * The `flash-linear-attention-npu-a3` 26.9.1 wheel in our container ships only `fla_npu.ops.triton.triton_core.causal_conv1d` fwd/bwd/states Triton kernels — no decode-path `causal_conv1d_update` (that lands with fla-npu PR [Doc] Update model support doc (add QwQ) for v0.7.3 #390 / [Feature][Ops] Migrate causal conv1d updates from fla-npu PR #390 #15341), so it cannot be bound as a drop-in today.
  * Decode engine flags (the failure needs this combination):
    * `speculative_config={'method': 'dspark', 'num_speculative_tokens': 5}`
    * `cudagraph_mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (+ `enable_npugraph_ex: True`, `async_scheduling`)
    * `max_num_batched_tokens: 400`, `max_num_seqs: 32`
  * Steps: start the 8 decode engines, wait until all 8 `/health` return 200, then send one request directly to a single decode DP rank (e.g. `POST decode_node:7100/v1/chat/completions`, `max_tokens=8`). The engine wedge (Phase 1) starts immediately; the GDN conv1d dummy-decode crash (Phase 2) follows a few minutes later and kills the remaining EngineCores. Reproduced twice (2026-10-10 07:22–07:55 UTC and 2026-10-11 09:16–09:33 UTC).

### Environment

  * vllm-ascend: `main` @ `05fa3be5f` (`0.19.1rc2.dev2688+g05fa3be5f`)
  * vllm: 0.30.0
  * torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, CANN 9.1.0, Ascend910 (A3, 910.93)

### Notes / related PRs

  * [Refactor][Ops] Remove causal_conv1d_update_npu #14620 removed the Triton `causal_conv1d_update_npu` kernel; the patch site in `patch_triton.py` still references it and always falls back.
  * [Feature] Enable CausalConv1dV2 operator on Ascend A3 #17250 (open) enables `aclnnCausalConv1dV2` on A3 — explicitly targets ACL-graph-unfriendly dynamic shapes (host-side `query_start_loc`, DSpark `num_accepted_tokens`) for the same conv1d path.
  * [wip]refactor(ops): remove deprecated GDN and causal_conv1d AscendC custom… #17629 (open, WIP) would switch GDN/KDA causal-conv1d callers to the fla_npu AscendC operators (incl. `causal_conv1d_update`).
  * [BugFix][Worker] Zero static KV buffers after cudagraph capture #17659 (merged after the affected build) fixes post-capture state corruption for GLM-5.3 KDA — different failure mode, does not fix this.

### Before submitting a new issue...

  * [Input] Did you search for existing issues? (searched `causal_conv1d`, `GDN`, `CausalConv1dBwd`, `conv1d decode`; no prior report of this failure)

     * vllm-ascend `releases/v0.30.0`: same exposure. `vllm_ascend/ops/causal_conv1d.py` is byte-identical to main (PyTorch impl; last commit `78f3a90f2` on both), the branch's `patch_triton.py` unconditionally binds that same PyTorch impl, and `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/causal_conv1d.py` there is a 430 B stub (only `extract_last_width`). So the v0.30.0 branch runs the same fallback — it just doesn't log the warning.
     * No merged or open PR fixes this. Open candidates that would: [Feature] Enable CausalConv1dV2 operator on Ascend A3 #17250 (`aclnnCausalConv1dV2` on A3 — host-side static metadata + DSpark `num_accepted_tokens`, directly targets ACL-graph-unfriendly dynamic shapes), [wip]refactor(ops): remove deprecated GDN and causal_conv1d AscendC custom… #17629 (switch GDN/KDA causal-conv1d callers to fla_npu `causal_conv1d_update`), [Feature][Ops] Migrate causal conv1d updates from fla-npu PR #390 #15341 / [Perf][Ops] AscendC causal_conv1d_update with small-pool staging #15430 (other NPU update-kernel migrations).
     * The `flash-linear-attention-npu-a3` 26.9.1 wheel in our container ships only `fla_npu.ops.triton.triton_core.causal_conv1d` fwd/bwd/states Triton kernels — no decode-path `causal_conv1d_update` (that lands with fla-npu PR [Doc] Update model support doc (add QwQ) for v0.7.3 #390 / [Feature][Ops] Migrate causal conv1d updates from fla-npu PR #390 #15341), so it cannot be bound as a drop-in today.

## Current mitigation on our side

     * Keep all traffic on the PD proxy path (P→D via MooncakeHybridConnector) — unaffected so far; direct-to-decode-rank requests are prohibited until a fix lands.
     * If direct access is unavoidable, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` cudagraph (or DSpark) must be disabled so the fallback never enters ACL graph capture.

Happy to test patches on our A3 cluster (2 nodes, DP8×TP2 decode, dspark×5, FULL_DECODE_ONLY).

Root cause for this batch (shared by #20214, #20216, #20218, #20220, #20221 — same CI run 40481333923):

PR #14620 (merged 2026-08-25, "[Refactor][Ops] Remove causal_conv1d_update_npu") deleted the kernel and "stopped monkey-patching vLLM's causal_conv1d_update", but left one binding attempt behind.

`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/causal_conv1d.py` is now a 14-line stub (`__all__ = ["PAD_SLOT_ID", "extract_last_width"]`), while `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_triton.py:336-352` still does:
    
    try:
        from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.mamba.causal_conv1d import causal_conv1d_update_npu as _cc1d_update_npu
        _cc1d.causal_conv1d_update = _cc1d_update_npu
        ...
    except Exception as _cc1d_err:
        logger.warning("NPU Triton causal_conv1d_update is unavailable (%s); falling back ... stalls ACL graph capture at decode-FULL.", _cc1d_err)

So the import always fails, and every run logs that WARNING — whose text now describes a fallback path that no longer exists after #14620.

Why removing the block is behaviour-neutral: the binding that actually takes effect is earlier in the same file (`_cc1d.causal_conv1d_update = _npu_causal_conv1d_update`, backed by `vllm_ascend/ops/causal_conv1d.py`), and it is unconditional. The deleted try/except could only ever override it when the import succeeded, which it cannot.

I have the 17-line deletion ready (no behaviour change, no new code). I cannot open the PR yet: my fork of this repo is a stale August snapshot, and syncing it is refused because the token lacks the `workflow` scope (the sync would touch `.github/workflows/_build_csrc_cache.yaml`). I will push the branch and link it here as soon as the fork is synced — or if someone with push access wants the patch in the meantime, it is a pure deletion of that block.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10 FAQ

For general installation and environment issues, refer to Public FAQs.

### Q1: Why does the service report OOM during startup or soon after accepting requests?

Check that the weight precision and device allocation match Section 3.1, and use `--quantization ascend` for the quantized examples. Reduce context length, concurrency, or batched tokens as needed, and leave runtime memory headroom when setting `--gpu-memory-utilization`. Follow the tuning order in Section 9.2.

### Q2: Why does multi-node MP deployment hang during initialization?

Verify connectivity using Section 3.2. Set `HCCL_IF_IP` to the selected NIC's IP and `HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME`/`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` to its interface name. Check the DP master address, matching RPC ports, non-overlapping rank ranges, and the worker node's `--headless` option against Section 5.2.

### Q3: Can I enable prefix caching in PD disaggregation?

The A3 PD, 950DT W4A8C8 PD, and A2 PD examples enable prefix caching. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
